Manhattan Bridge — material and arrangement evidence — photo review

Give each photograph every category it can actually inform — one view of a tower is often masonry, a cornice and a cable anchorage at once. Tick skip for anything not worth keeping. Untouched photographs stay auto_screened and are treated as weaker evidence.
A photograph can establish what something is made of and how it is arranged. It cannot give a dimension without scale control. Tick a category for what the image shows, not for what you hope to measure from it.
masonry
Anchorage and pier stonework close enough to tell the stone and see the coursing. MAT-010 was promoted to B on photographic evidence of dressed coursed ashlar; the anchorage arch barrel (MAT-022) rests on the same kind of reading. Feeds OQ-019.
arch
The anchorage thoroughfare arch and the tower arch openings. OQ-023 and OQ-024: these are modelled from a photograph rather than a dimension, so more photographs can confirm the FORM even though none of them may set the springing height.
truss
A transverse or oblique view of the stiffening trusses. OQ-017: the diagonal direction at each panel and the member sections are unregistered, and the web is currently drawn as lines rather than members (OQ-021). A photograph cannot measure a chord, but it can show which way the diagonals lean.
cable
Main cables, suspenders and cable bands. OQ-019 lists the cables among the unregistered materials; CONF-001 is an unresolved conflict over cable diameter that a photograph cannot settle but can at least illustrate.
approach
The approach viaducts from below or beside. OQ-020: the structural form is unregistered -- the model draws placeholder bents, and SRC-024 suggests a deck truss. This is the category that settles what actually carries the approaches.
deck
Roadway surfaces and their framing. OQ-019 names both roadway surfaces as unregistered materials.
rail
The four subway tracks on the lower deck and their supporting structure. OQ-010: the exact transverse centrelines are unregistered. A photograph shows the arrangement and the track structure without measuring the gauge separation.
portal
The Manhattan approach portal and its ornament. Modelled from very little; anything showing what is actually there is useful.
context
A good overall view that shows the bridge in its setting but settles no single component. Useful for the presentation layer, weak as evidence.
measurable frame
A frame that could be MEASURED, not just read. Tick it when a known dimension is fully visible in the same plane as the thing of interest and the view is roughly square on -- above all a complete rail pair, which is 4 ft 8.5 in by forced standard (CTL-017) and so is a ruler lying in the photograph. Both rail pairs AND both trusses in one square-ish frame is the shot that retires CTL-105 and CTL-106. This tick does not itself grant a dimension; it marks the frame as a candidate for photogrammetric measurement under CONFIDENCE-MODEL.md section 6.2, which is the only route by which a photograph reaches grade B for a length.
